assertions.name: bond_strengthens_from_z1_to_z2
assertions.source: w(2)/w(1); the entire content of b3 > 0, per lt_of_b3_pos

assertions.name: single_ratio_scaling_refuted
assertions.unit: relative disagreement between the two measured ratios
assertions.source: eps(z)=eps(1)*r^(z-1) requires w(2)/w(1) = w(3)/w(2); they differ by ~44%, refuting the family for every r, convention-independently

assertions.name: su4_support_bound_locates_the_turnover
assertions.source: dim[1^n] = C(4,n) vanishes for n >= 5, so the fully antisymmetric spin-isospin regime ends at A=4; the measured eps peak is at A=4. A SUPPORT bound (C(4,n)=0), NOT a positivity claim -- an earlier probe's C(4,n)>0 sign argument was wrong and is not reused.

assertions.name: same_orbital_fraction_fails_beyond_A7
assertions.unit: verdict (1 = close below A=7 and refuted above, as claimed)
assertions.source: normalised at the alpha (one parameter); <8% for A=5,6,7 then >20% at A=9 and >70% at A=12. Recorded as a scope-(a) negative: this model ALONE does not reproduce w, which does not exclude the ingredient from a multi-term closure.

description: Measures the non-transferability the b3 > 0 rise requires, and tests candidate mechanisms for the rise and the alpha turnover. Refutes the single-ratio (Markov-power) scaling family and the same-orbital-fraction law; locates the turnover at A=4 from the SU(4) [1^n] support bound C(4,n) = 0 for n >= 5, without predicting its height. Derives no magnitude.

scope.what_is_proved_elsewhere: the NEGATIVE half: QOU.Mass.UniformBondSimpleGraphExclusion shows no uniform-bond simple-graph assembly can give the rise, for any graph family (a simple graph on 3 vertices has at most 3 edges)
what_is_refuted_here: single-ratio scaling eps(z) = eps(1)*r^(z-1), for EVERY r (the two measured ratios differ by ~44%) -- kills the simplest form of the Markov-power mechanism, convention-independently
scope.what_survives: the turnover LOCATION at A=4 from the SU(4) [1^n] support bound C(4,n)=0 for n>=5 -- parameter-free, but it locates only, and it rests on Wigner's symmetry-to-binding assumption which this corpus does not derive
scope.still_open: the SIZE of the rise: why eps(2)/eps(1) = 1.2137 and eps(3)/eps(1) = 2.1200. No mechanism tested here predicts either number.
